name: Eric Hafner
bio: Eric Hafner is a registered Democrat who advanced from Alaska's 2026 top-four primary for the U.S. House after other candidates withdrew; he also appeared on the 2024 general election ballot for the seat and ran earlier for Congress in Hawaii and Oregon. He is serving a 20-year federal prison sentence in New York after pleading guilty in 2022 to making threats, and has no documented ties to Alaska.

platform.point: Says Alaska resources such as ANWR should not be used for short-term exploitation amid an environmental crisis.
His 2024 campaign flyer called for preserving fisheries and greener alternatives to oil drilling and mineral mining.
Says war should be avoided at all costs.
Backs broad access to education and higher education, including teaching Indigenous and Black history.
Lists work with groups seeking to reform drug laws and promote harm reduction.

economy.evidence: His official election statement lists active support for the Fight for $15 minimum wage campaign and a teachers' union.

liberty.evidence: Abortion: says women should have the right to their own medical choices; drugs: backs reforming drug laws and harm reduction; speech: objects to limits on which books people read.

foreign.evidence: General statement in his official election pamphlet that war should be avoided at all costs.

energy.evidence: General statement in his election pamphlet that resources like ANWR should not be used for short-term exploitation amid an environmental crisis.

education.evidence: General statement backing education for all, plus listed support for K-12 public education campaigns with a teachers' union.

notes: Positions come mainly from his 2026 Alaska Division of Elections pamphlet statement; he left the iVoterGuide questionnaire blank and has no campaign website. Immigration, welfare, security, tech and faith remain unknown, and coverage says his eligibility may face a residency challenge.

name: Shomari Figures
bio: Shomari Figures is a Mobile native and attorney who has represented Alabama's 2nd District since January 2025. He previously worked in the Obama White House, as legislative counsel to Senator Sherrod Brown, and as deputy chief of staff to Attorney General Merrick Garland. He serves on the House Agriculture Committee.

platform.point: Opposes Medicaid cuts and supports expanding Medicaid in Alabama.
Co-introduced the bipartisan Rural Hospital Stabilization Act and secured funding for rural hospitals in the district.
Sponsored the Made in America Jobs Act to support projects that bring foreign jobs back to the U.S.
Proposed tax relief for new parents and for children's enrichment activities.
Secured federal water and wastewater funding for communities in the district.
Voted against the 2025 Republican tax and budget law, saying it favored the wealthy and added to the debt.
Offered an amendment to keep states from bearing new SNAP costs; it was rejected.
Introduced a bill to undo the administration's foreign beef import plan and require tariffs on beef imports.

economy.evidence: Voted against the 2025 tax law, saying it gave millionaires large tax breaks, and sponsored the Made in America Jobs Act on reshoring.

welfare.evidence: Opposes Medicaid cuts, supports Medicaid expansion and federal aid to rural hospitals.

immigration.evidence: Voted for the Laken Riley Act requiring detention of certain arrested noncitizens.

foreign.evidence: Voted in July 2025 against an amendment to strike $500 million in U.S.-Israel missile defense funding, which failed 6-422.

notes: Searched House roll calls, press releases and Wikipedia; GENIUS Act vote is roll call 200 (2025). Campaign website not confirmed, and no clear record was found on abortion, guns, policing, energy, school choice or religion.

name: Lee McInnis
current_role: Retired defense intelligence officer and educator
bio: Lee McInnis is an Alabama native who served six years in Army intelligence and 28 years in the defense intelligence community, including with special operations in Afghanistan. After retiring he taught communications and American government. He holds a master's degree in history from Auburn University.

platform.point: Says the economy should work for working families and the wealthiest should pay their fair share.
Wants health care access for all and more hospitals, pediatricians and mental health services in the district.
Pledges to refuse corporate and foreign PAC money and hold regular town halls.
Criticizes SNAP and health program cuts in the 2025 budget law.
Opposes current deportation operations while backing modern border security, faster vetting and longer H-2A and H-2B work visas.
Opposes dismantling the Department of Education and questions whether Alabama's CHOOSE Act vouchers help vulnerable students.
Makes the case for a living wage for working families.
Wants defense money spent on modern capabilities such as drones rather than costly legacy weapons systems.

economy.evidence: General statements that the ultra-wealthy should pay their fair share of taxes and that workers need a living wage.

welfare.evidence: Calls for health care for all and opposes SNAP and health cuts.

security.evidence: His campaign site, as quoted by Branch, backs requiring federal agents to display their names and agency and banning face coverings on duty.

immigration.evidence: Calls current deportation operations inhumane and wants longer guest-worker visas set by economic need, while also backing modern border security.

education.evidence: Opposes dismantling the Department of Education, supports free public education for every child and questions Alabama's CHOOSE Act vouchers.

notes: Read the campaign home page and blog posts on immigration, education and defense, plus news coverage; his defense posts criticize the Iran war's conduct and procurement but do not fit the foreign-policy scale. No stated positions were found on abortion, guns, energy, tech or religion.

name: Maurice Mercer
current_role: Business account executive; former Pelham City Council president
bio: Maurice Mercer served on the Pelham City Council from 2012 to 2025, including four years as council president, and was the first Black person elected to office in the city. He is a business account executive at Spectrum Business, a former union organizer and a Troy University alumnus. He won the Democratic nomination for Alabama's 6th District in the August 2026 special primary.

platform.point: Campaigns on lowering everyday costs for families.
Prioritizes making health care more affordable.
Supports continued federal infrastructure investment, including rail projects.
Describes unions as central to giving workers a voice and fair wages.
Pledges to stand up for veterans and work toward bringing troops home.

economy.evidence: Supports continued federal infrastructure investment, including rail, and describes labor unions as the backbone of the working class.

foreign.evidence: General campaign statement about working toward bringing U.S. troops home.

notes: Searched his campaign site (no issues page), BirminghamWatch, 1819 News and other race coverage; Shelby County Reporter and Coosa County News blocked access. No positions were found on immigration, abortion, guns, energy, tech, education or religion, and his city council votes were not reviewed.

name: Ammie Akin
bio: Ammie Akin is a Birmingham-area educator who has worked as a classroom teacher, assistant superintendent for Trussville City Schools and a college professor who trains school leaders. She holds a special education degree from the University of Alabama and a Doctor of Education from Samford University, co-founded the Hub in the Hills nonprofit workspace and chairs the board of Unless U, which serves adults with disabilities. She won the Republican nomination in the August 2026 special primary for Alabama's 7th District.

platform.point: Wants to cut wasteful federal spending and restore fiscal responsibility.
Aims to reduce regulatory burdens so Alabama businesses can grow.
Seeks better rural health care access and keeping rural hospitals open.
Supports agriculture, timber and broadband expansion to grow rural communities.
Promotes education improvement through partnerships among educators, parents and communities.
Wants law enforcement and the military to have the resources they need.
Wants every student prepared for college, a career or another path.

economy.evidence: General statements about cutting red tape and wasteful federal spending.

security.evidence: General statement that law enforcement should get the resources it needs.

notes: Read her campaign home and issues pages plus BirminghamWatch, Alabama Gazette and Yellowhammer coverage; her platform names broad priorities only. No stated positions were found on abortion, guns, immigration, school choice, energy, tech, foreign policy or religion.

name: Everett Wess
bio: Everett W. Wess is a Birmingham attorney who has led The Wess Law Firm since 2001 and served eight years as a Midfield municipal court judge. He has also worked as a prosecutor, public defender and technology professional supporting NASA operations in Huntsville. He is state president of the Alabama New South Coalition and holds degrees from Alabama A&M University and Birmingham School of Law.

platform.point: Supports affordable healthcare with more funding for rural medical providers and underserved hospitals.
Links economic growth to quality public education and workforce development.
Calls for fair courts, clean government and equal access to the justice system.
Prioritizes protecting voting rights and community protections.
Criticizes 2025 Medicaid cuts and pledges to strengthen rural hospitals, emergency services, and maternal and mental health care.
Pledges to lower prescription drug costs.
Opposes the administration's foreign beef import plan and backs a bill requiring tariffs on beef imports.

economy.evidence: Backs a bill to undo foreign beef imports and require tariffs on them to protect Alabama cattle producers.

welfare.evidence: Opposes the Medicaid cuts in the 2025 budget law, notes Alabama's refusal to expand Medicaid, and wants more federal support for rural hospitals.

education.evidence: General campaign statement emphasizing quality public education as the basis for jobs and workforce development.

notes: Searched the campaign site, Vote-USA, Branch and Alabama Reflector (blocked), plus Alabama Political Reporter coverage of his blog posts. No stated positions were found on abortion, guns, immigration, foreign policy, energy, tech, policing or religion.

name: Terri Yarbrough Green
bio: Terri Yarbrough Green is a board-certified pathologist and former laboratory medical director whose career included work at rural hospitals. Born in El Paso, she lives in Paragould, Arkansas, and earned degrees from Baylor University and the University of Texas Health Science Center at San Antonio. She is a first-time candidate challenging Rep. Rick Crawford.

platform.point: Uphold the rule of law, equal justice and checks and balances.
Remove dark money from politics and ensure free, fair and transparent elections.
Support family farms and push back on large agricultural monopolies.
Raise the minimum wage.
Expand access to affordable health care, including maternity care closer to home.
Improve infrastructure and broadband.
Opposes Medicaid work requirements and SNAP changes in the 2025 budget law.
Opposes the war with Iran and says the Obama-era nuclear agreement had been slowing uranium enrichment.

economy.evidence: Supports raising the minimum wage and backing family farms against agricultural consolidation.

welfare.evidence: Calls for expanding affordable health care and opposes the Medicaid work requirements in the 2025 budget law.

foreign.evidence: Opposes the current war with Iran and favors the diplomatic nuclear agreement reached under Obama.

notes: Campaign materials use the name Terri Green; searched her site and Talk Business and Democrat-Gazette coverage. No positions were found on abortion, guns, immigration, energy, tech, education or religion.

name: Jonathan Nez
current_role: Former President of the Navajo Nation
bio: Jonathan Nez served as President of the Navajo Nation from 2019 to 2023, as Vice President from 2015 to 2019 and as a Navajo Nation Council delegate from 2007 to 2015. Born in Tuba City, he studied political science and public administration at Northern Arizona University. He was the 2024 Democratic nominee for Arizona's 2nd District and is running again in 2026.

platform.point: Aims to lower health care, housing and utility costs for families.
Pledges to protect Arizona water security and invest in affordable, healthy food.
Wants long-term rural infrastructure, support for farmers and ranchers, and disaster protection.
Promises to take on government corruption and money in politics.
Commits to protecting tribal sovereignty and voting rights.
Opposes proposed cuts to Head Start and shifting the program to state control.
Opposes continued U.S. spending on the war with Iran, citing costs to Arizona families.
Reaffirmed support for Arizona workers and labor unions.

economy.evidence: General statements that the economy should put working families ahead of billionaires and criticism of tax cuts for the wealthy.

welfare.evidence: Defends federal Head Start funding for low-income children and wants to protect coverage for pre-existing conditions and lower drug costs.

liberty.evidence: LGBTQ rights: endorsed legalizing same-sex marriage on the Navajo Nation in 2022.

immigration.evidence: In 2024 said immigration needs fixing and backed the bipartisan Senate border bill that failed that year.

foreign.evidence: Opposes continued U.S. involvement in the war with Iran, citing its costs to Arizona families.

education.evidence: Opposes cuts to federally funded Head Start and moving it to state control, saying every child deserves quality education.

faith.evidence: General statement: urged leaders to favor prayer and unity and quoted scripture in a campaign statement.

notes: Read the campaign issues and news pages, Wikipedia and Navajo Times coverage; a Center Square debate report on abortion and immigration was paywalled. No clear record was found on energy, tech, policing or guns.
